display.title: Episode 373: The Secret of the Empty Fireplace (Yahrzeit of the Tzemach Tzedek)
display.summary_short: On the eve of Pesach: the matzah as food of faith and healing, what a yahrzeit means, and how young Menachem Mendel hid in a fireplace to hear the Alter Rebbe teach.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on 13 Nissan 5749, the day before Erev Pesach and the yahrzeit of the Tzemach Tzedek. Uncle Yossi looks forward to the two Seder nights: to really feel the freedom of 'zman cheiruseinu', as one of the Twelve Pesukim teaches, children should take part in everything, the wine, the four questions, the matzah and the maror. Above all, make sure to eat matzah on both nights; the Arizal calls it food of faith and food of healing. After a Pesach Hakochainik march to 'Mi Mitzrayim Ge'altanu', a four-year-old leads the Shema. Uncle Yossi then explains a yahrzeit: all a person's Torah and mitzvos are added up on the day the neshamah returns to Hashem, and that light shines again every year, so we add in Torah and mitzvos on a tzaddik's yahrzeit. The story: nine-year-old Menachem Mendel, too young to join his grandfather the Alter Rebbe's lessons, hides in the empty fireplace between the two rooms to listen. One cold evening the fire is lit while he is inside, absorbed in the Torah; he is pulled out and only wakes when the Alter Rebbe places a hand on his head. The show ends with how the whole family takes part in bedikas chametz and a reminder to invite guests to the Seder.
display.lesson: Love Torah so much that you will do anything to learn more; and on a tzaddik's yahrzeit, add in Torah, mitzvos and good midos.
